bridge.name: Bridge
bridge.good: Solid underfoot, no wobble. Abutments whole, railings firm, decking sound, nothing piled against it upstream.
bridge.also: Also: wobble when walked on, debris upstream, a hazard tree over it, a slick deck.
bridge.unsafe: Don't use it. The Local Chair is told the moment it uploads.
bridge.rule: Don't repair a bridge yourself. Log it; the Local Chair takes it from there.
bridge.sources: NYNJTC Trail Maintenance Manual 8.5 · NYNJTC Bridge Best Practices · ATC Stream Crossings and Bridges

puncheon.name: Puncheon
puncheon.good: Level, not sunk, swept of leaves, with grip on the boards. Inspect it exactly like a bridge.
checks: Slick, leaves or mud on the deck
puncheon.unsafe: Same as a bridge: don't use it, and the Local Chair is told when it uploads.
puncheon.rule: Don't fix it, log it. Re-levelling a sunk sleeper is the maintainer's job.
puncheon.sources: NYNJTC Trail Maintenance Manual 8.5 · NYNJTC Natural Surface Trail Building · ATC Trail Condition & Assessment

shelter.name: Shelter
shelter.good: Wood off the ground, a roof that overhangs, one small fire ring, litter-free, side trails blazed.
checks: Roof leaking, sagging or missing shingles
Floor, walls or deck rotten or broken
Fire ring: more than one, oversized, full of ash
Food storage (box, cables, pole) missing or broken
A hazard tree over the site
shelter.also: Also: graffiti, litter, vents, chimney, retaining walls, signs.
shelter.unsafe: Don't sleep in it. A Poor or Unsafe shelter also raises a Shelter repair report for the crew.
shelter.rule: A hazard tree over the site comes first (ATC). Log it; a crew removes it.
shelter.sources: ATC Overnight Site Planning Guidance · ATC shelter inventory form · NYNJTC Trail Maintenance Manual 8.5

privy.name: Privy
privy.good: A moldering privy: slatted cribs above ground, a full bin of shavings, an earthy smell, sealed against animals.
checks: Crib full, or a cone to knock down
privy.also: Also: wipes and wrappers inside, which don't compost.
privy.unsafe: A floor or seat that can't be used. Everything else is Poor.
privy.rule: Never add lime (ATC). Restocking shavings is the maintainer's job; just log the empty bin.
privy.sources: ATC: It's a dirty job · ATC Backcountry Sanitation Manual · ATC privy inventory form · NYNJTC Trail Maintenance Manual 8.5

campsite.name: Campsite
campsite.good: Sites 200 ft from water, one formal fire ring per site, tent pads 8 by 8 ft or bigger, no spreading.
checks: Extra fire rings that visitors built
Ring oversized, or built up with ash
Site spreading: new paths, trampled plants
campsite.also: Also: burned trash in the ring.
campsite.unsafe: A hazard tree over a tent site. Otherwise a campsite is Poor at worst.
campsite.rule: Count the rings and photograph them. Scattering an illegal ring is the maintainer's job (NYNJTC).
campsite.sources: ATC Overnight Site Planning Guidance · ATC Fire Ring Management · ATC campsite inventory form · NYNJTC Trail Maintenance Manual 8.5

water.name: Water source
water.good: Left natural or lightly improved, blue blazes and a treat-all-water sign, the side trail well marked.
checks: Blue blazes or the sign missing
Something could foul it: a privy or camp across the stream
water.unsafe: Not for a bad smell or colour: nobody is in danger from the structure. Write what you suspect in the note.
water.rule: The club tests a suspect source with ATC's help. A confirmed one comes off the maps.
water.sources: ATC Drinking Water policy · ATC Overnight Site Planning Guidance · ATC Backcountry Sanitation Manual · NYNJTC Trail Maintenance Manual 8.5

blaze.name: Blaze
blaze.good: White, 2 by 6 in, sharp corners, eye height, usually on the right. From each one you can see the next.
checks: Faded, flaking, damaged or the wrong shape
Can't see the next one from here
Leaves or brush across the sightline
An old blaze never sprayed out
blaze.unsafe: A blaze is never Unsafe. If you can't see the next one, that's Poor, and the maintainer should hear about it.
blaze.rule: Repainting is the maintainer's job, above 50°F (NYNJTC). You log it.
blaze.sources: ATC Marking the Trail · NYNJTC Trail Maintenance Manual 8.5 · NYNJTC Guidelines for Blazing Trails

sign.name: Sign
sign.good: Mounted high on a 4 by 4 post with an angled top, fastened so it can't be backed out, still true.
checks: Out of date, or a temporary sign left up
Flyers, ads or stickers on it
sign.unsafe: A sign is never Unsafe. Log a damaged or missing one as Poor.
sign.rule: Nobody puts up or replaces a sign on their own (NYNJTC). Log it; the Local Chair takes it from there.
sign.sources: ATC Trail Signs policy · NYNJTC Trail Maintenance Manual 8.5 · NYNJTC Trail Volunteer Worksheet

kiosk.name: Kiosk
kiosk.good: Panels behind a locked Lexan cover, a map with you-are-here, emergency info, Leave No Trace, a sound roof.
checks: Roof or posts damaged, rotten, leaning
A sign that should be on it and isn't
kiosk.unsafe: A kiosk that could fall on someone. Everything else is Poor.
kiosk.rule: Outdated content is worse than none (ATC). The Local Chair sends one photo a year to ATC.
kiosk.sources: ATC trailhead kiosks guidance (2012) · NYNJTC Trail Maintenance Manual 8.5

parking.name: Parking
parking.good: Small, clean, safe and well marked: four to six cars, visible from the road, the trailhead easy to spot.
checks: Trailhead hard to find from the lot
Cars on an unsafe pull-off outside the lot
parking.unsafe: Only if the lot itself is dangerous: an entrance washed out, a tree down across it.
parking.rule: Count the cars every visit. ATC asks for average and peak-weekend counts.
parking.sources: ATC Trailheads and Parking policy · NYNJTC Trail Maintenance Manual 8.5 · NYNJTC Pocket Guide

steps.name: Steps
steps.good: Each stone locked in behind the one below, flat faces up, low rises, water running off, swept of leaves.
checks: Stone loose, missing, settled or eroded
steps.also: Also: checkdams and waterbars nearby with rotten or missing wood.
steps.unsafe: A rocking step on a steep pitch. The Local Chair is told when it uploads.
steps.rule: Water pooling on a step means it needs resetting: log it (NYNJTC).
steps.sources: NYNJTC Trail Maintenance Manual 8.5 · NYNJTC Natural Surface Trail Building · ATC Keeping Hikers on the Centerline

other.name: Something else
other.good: Water bars, checkdams, drainage dips and cairns: small things a crew built that keep water and hikers where they belong.
checks: Water bar clogged on the uphill side, or its outlet blocked
Water bar walked around, or with no downhill exit
Cairn knocked down, or a visitor's rock stack where none belongs
other.also: Also here: culverts, stiles, gates, register boxes, walls. Just say what it is.
other.unsafe: Rarely: a collapsed wall or crossing. A clogged water bar is Poor.
other.rule: If a crew built it, log it. If the trail itself is going wrong, that's Report a problem.
other.sources: ATC Condition Assessment Report form · ATC Trail Alignment and Water · ATC Keeping Hikers on the Centerline · NYNJTC Trail Maintenance Manual 8.5
